per_query.query_text: UE keeps reselecting to 3G even when LTE coverage is adequate
per_query.reference: Idle-mode reselection to 3G when LTE is available is driven by cell selection/reselection parameters. Check: (1) SIB3/SIB5 — thresh-X-high and thresh-X-low for inter-RAT reselection. (2) RSRP of serving LTE cell — if below s-IntraSearchP the UE starts measuring neighbours. (3) IRAT priority configuration — if 3G cells have higher absolute priority they will be selected. (4) UE capability — is VoLTE supported? If not, UE may be configured to prefer UTRAN for CS domain. Review idle-mode measurement parameters in RRC SIB broadcast.
per_query.prediction: UE drains battery faster than expected. Possible: (1) DRX not configured well - UE not sleeping. (2) Poor coverage forces max TX power. (3) Constant network reselection due to low RSRP. (4) Application keeping radio active (chatty heartbeats). (5) No RRC Release after idle - eNB keeping UE connected. Review DRX params and eNB inactivity timers.

per_query.query_text: Secondary cell addition for carrier aggregation fails silently
per_query.reference: When SCell addition fails without explicit failure: (1) Check RRCConnectionReconfiguration — is SCell configuration present and UE-NR/UE-EUTRA-Capability confirming CA band combination support? (2) Verify SCell is in the active neighbour relation list of PCell. (3) SCell RSRP threshold for addition (A4/A6 event configuration). (4) X2 interface between cells — SCell addition uses X2 for load information. (5) SCell scheduler load — may reject addition if PRB utilization is too high. Check eNB counters for CA addition attempts vs successes.
per_query.prediction: NSA requires LTE anchor + NR secondary cell. Checks: (1) UE 5G capability reported in Attach (UE-NR-Capability IE). (2) LTE anchor cell has X2 to gNB. (3) B1 measurement event configured for NR. (4) SgNB Addition Request succeeds over Xn/X2. (5) UE in coverage of both LTE and NR simultaneously.

per_query.query_text: PDCP SDU discard rate spiking on uplink for one cell sector
per_query.reference: High PDCP discard indicates packets are being dropped before transmission due to buffer overflow or discard timer expiry. Steps: (1) Check uplink SINR — poor radio quality causes HARQ retransmissions that back up the PDCP buffer. (2) UE transmit power headroom (PHR) — if UE is power-limited it cannot retransmit. (3) Uplink scheduler — is UE getting sufficient resource grants? (4) PDCP discard timer configuration — may be too aggressive. (5) Check for uplink interference source (PIM, external). Correlate with HARQ BLER and PHR statistics in the RRM counters.
per_query.prediction: HARQ BLER target typically 10% first transmission, <1% after 4 retransmissions. If poor: (1) UE TX power limited (check PHR reports). (2) Uplink SINR low due to interference. (3) PUSCH allocation too aggressive (high MCS for the SINR). (4) Timing advance error. Link budget analysis with scheduler logs finds the culprit.

per_query.query_text: Dedicated bearer for streaming video keeps being deactivated mid-session
per_query.reference: Non-GBR dedicated bearer teardown mid-session: (1) Check PCRF policy — is a Gx CCA-Update removing the bearer? TDF detection may be reclassifying traffic. (2) Inactivity timer on PGW for dedicated bearers — may be misconfigured. (3) SGW/PGW resource limits — bearer table exhaustion causes eviction. (4) UE-initiated bearer modification (QoS downgrade request). (5) Check ESM cause in Deactivate EPS Bearer Context Request. Trace the Gx interface for PCC rule changes correlated with bearer deactivation timestamps.
per_query.prediction: Post-dial delay >3s is noticeable. Contributors: (1) DNS lookup for called number ENUM. (2) SIP INVITE routing hops (P-CSCF -> S-CSCF -> AS chain). (3) HSS Sh interface slow for user profile. (4) Dedicated bearer activation adds ~200ms for QCI 1. (5) Precondition negotiation per 3GPP profile. Measure each hop with correlated logs.

per_query.query_text: GTPv2-C signaling delay between MME and SGW causing session setup lag
per_query.reference: GTPv2-C (S11) delay causes PDN setup latency. Investigate: (1) Round-trip time on S11 path — run pings between MME and SGW loopback addresses. (2) SGW processing delay — check SGW CPU and message queue depth during busy hour. (3) Retransmissions on GTPv2-C — if Create Session Request is retransmitted, S11 RTT exceeds the T3-RESPONSE timer (default 3s). (4) IP routing asymmetry on the S11 VLAN. (5) SGW pool load balancing — one SGW may be overloaded. Use wireshark/tshark with GTP dissector to measure per-message RTT on the S11 interface.
per_query.prediction: GTP-U over UDP 2152. Drops: (1) MTU issues - if packets fragmented and reassembly fails. (2) UDP checksum errors. (3) TEID mismatch - session state divergence. (4) Firewall stateful inspection breaking flow. (5) ECMP hash flapping causing out-of-order. Capture GTP with tshark, check sequence numbers per TEID.

per_query.query_text: SRVCC handover from VoLTE to WCDMA failing during active call
per_query.reference: SRVCC (Single Radio Voice Call Continuity) failure: (1) Verify SVP (Sv) interface between MME and MSC-Server is up. (2) Check PS-to-CS handover trigger — B2 measurement event must fire with WCDMA threshold configured. (3) WCDMA cell must be in UE's active neighbour set (verify UTRAN frequency list in SIB6). (4) STN-SR (Session Transfer Number for SR-VCC) must be provisioned in HSS. (5) IMS ATU-STI (Access Transfer Update) must complete before WCDMA bearer is established. Check MME SRVCC counters — failure cause codes (e.g. target cell unavailable, Sv timeout) will narrow the root cause.
per_query.prediction: CSFB redirects to UTRAN. Failures: (1) SRVCC not actually needed here - this is CSFB, check SGs path. (2) No UTRAN coverage at UE location. (3) Gs interface between SGSN and MSC down. (4) Location Update to MSC fails (IMSI not in VLR). (5) MSC paging timer expires before UE completes RAU. Logs on MSC show final cause.

per_query.query_text: Gx interface timeout causing all new bearer requests to be rejected
per_query.reference: Gx (PCRF interface) timeout blocks all dynamic PCC rule delivery. Steps: (1) Check Diameter routing — is the CCR-I reaching the PCRF? Verify Diameter realm routing on the DRA. (2) PCRF health — CPU, memory, SPR backend response time. (3) CCR timeout value on PGW — if shorter than PCRF processing time, spurious timeouts occur. (4) Check if PGW is configured with a default-rule fallback for Gx timeout (local policy). If not, all sessions requiring dynamic policy will fail. (5) Capture Diameter traffic on Gx — look for CCA response codes (5012 = Unable to Deliver). Immediate mitigation: enable local PCC fallback on PGW.
per_query.prediction: Service Request by UE transitioning IDLE->CONNECTED. Failures: (1) Authentication failed (SIM sync issue). (2) Security mode command failed. (3) NAS count mismatch - common after abnormal release. (4) Bearer establishment fails (see ESM cause). Aggregate by EMM cause on MME to find pattern.

per_query.query_text: NAS reject EMM cause 11 affecting subset of inbound roaming subscribers
per_query.reference: EMM cause 11 (PLMN not allowed) from MME during roaming: (1) Check VPLMN's allowed-PLMN list in MME — HPLMN PLMN ID may be missing. (2) OCS/PCRF roaming profile — subscription may not allow this service type for the HPLMN. (3) HSS ULA (Update Location Answer) flags — check 'PLMN-ODB' bit (Operator Determined Barring). (4) Roaming agreement active and reflected in systems? (5) Does it affect all IMSI ranges from that HPLMN or a subset (may indicate partial profile migration). Correlate MME EMM reject cause codes with specific HPLMN MCC-MNC pairs.
per_query.prediction: Service Request by UE transitioning IDLE->CONNECTED. Failures: (1) Authentication failed (SIM sync issue). (2) Security mode command failed. (3) NAS count mismatch - common after abnormal release. (4) Bearer establishment fails (see ESM cause). Aggregate by EMM cause on MME to find pattern.

per_query.query_text: eNB not generating handover decision despite UE sending A3 measurement reports
per_query.reference: When A3 events are received but no handover is initiated: (1) Verify A3 offset and hysteresis — if configured too aggressively the UE may trigger A3 but the source eNB disagrees. (2) Check neighbour relation — target cell must be in ANR table with valid PCI and EARFCN. (3) Target cell load rejection — X2 HO Request may be rejected by target due to high PRB utilization. (4) X2 interface health between source and target eNB — HO request may never reach the target. (5) Time-to-trigger (TTT) — is A3 event sustained for the full TTT before handover is attempted? Enable RRC trace on the source eNB to verify HO decision logic.
per_query.prediction: High RRC re-est rate = UEs losing RRC connection (radio link failure) and trying to resume. Indicates: (1) Coverage holes - UEs moving out of range. (2) Interference bursts. (3) Too-aggressive handover parameters causing HOF. (4) eNB software issue dropping contexts. Target <1% of total connections; >3% needs investigation.

per_query.query_text: TCP sessions over SGi dropped after exactly 5 minutes of inactivity
per_query.reference: Exact 5-minute TCP idle teardown is a firewall or NAT timeout. (1) Check CGNAT / stateful firewall TCP idle timeout on SGi — default is often 300s (5 min). Extend or set application-specific timeout. (2) PGW session idle timer — not typical for TCP but confirm SGW/PGW inactive session timeout. (3) Load balancer session persistence timer. (4) Application keepalive — if TCP keepalive is not configured, the 5-minute idle hits. Fix: increase firewall TCP idle timer or enable SO_KEEPALIVE on the application. Capture RST origin (client vs server vs CGNAT) with tshark on SGi to confirm.
per_query.prediction: TCP RSTs from operator side to internet. Causes: (1) Session table overflow on CGNAT - flow evicted. (2) Firewall TCP idle timeout shorter than app keepalive. (3) Load balancer re-hashing. (4) MTU/MSS issues causing fragmentation drop then RST. (5) DPI injecting RST for policy violation. Capture on SGi will show RST origin.

per_query.query_text: Uplink noise floor elevated on 3 contiguous PRBs suggesting narrowband interference
per_query.reference: Narrowband interference on specific PRBs is typically external RF or PIM. Steps: (1) Use spectrum analyzer or eNB uplink interference counters to confirm the affected frequency range. (2) PIM check: contiguous PRB pattern near downlink carriers is PIM signature — run PIM sweep on jumpers, connectors, and antennas. (3) External narrowband interferer (e.g. LTE-M device, IoT gateway) — use direction-finding / spectrum scan. (4) Check if interference is time-correlated (burst vs constant) to identify source type. (5) Inter-cell interference — verify ICIC is configured, check if neighbouring cell uses same PRBs at full power.
per_query.prediction: PIM signature: uplink interference showing as elevated noise floor at specific frequencies = f(downlink carriers). Steps: (1) Use sweep/PIM tester on site. (2) Check connectors, weatherproofing, loose hardware. (3) Look for rusted metal objects near antennas (guy wires, bolts). (4) Verify jumper cable quality. PIM typically worsens with power/load.

per_query.query_text: S1-AP reset PDU storm from one eNB causing MME instability
per_query.reference: Repeated S1-AP RESET from one eNB destabilizes MME UE context. (1) Identify cause IE in RESET — does eNB report an internal failure, radio link failure, or transport? (2) Check eNB hardware alarms — baseband restarts cause SCTP association reset. (3) Transport flap: SCTP heartbeat failures trigger RESET. Check interface counters on both sides. (4) Software issue on eNB — scheduled restart? Check OMC for maintenance windows. (5) MME-side mitigation: implement RESET rate limiting per eNB. Isolate the problematic eNB from the pool temporarily to protect the MME from context churn. Pull SCTP statistics and eNB alarm history from OMC.
per_query.prediction: SCTP underpins S1-AP. Failures: (1) INIT chunk blocked by firewall (SCTP protocol 132). (2) Asymmetric routing breaking multi-homed paths. (3) Heartbeat interval mismatch. (4) Path MTU discovery issues with DF bit. (5) sctpdump on MME to see INIT/INIT-ACK. Most networks use single-homed SCTP to avoid multi-homing complexity.

per_query.query_text: eSIM remote provisioning fails at LPA profile download with HTTP 403
per_query.reference: LPA (Local Profile Assistant) HTTP 403 during SM-DP+ profile download: (1) Activation code or confirmation code mismatch — re-check against SM-DP+ portal. (2) SMDP certificate not trusted by device — verify root CA chain. (3) Device EID not whitelisted in SM-DP+ operator profile. (4) Order state machine issue: profile may already be in 'downloaded' or 'released' state in SM-DP+ — check order status via M2M or consumer API. (5) Network connectivity: LPA uses HTTPS to SM-DP+ address — check DNS resolution and firewall rules on the device connection. Collect LPA logs (AT+CSIM or vendor diagnostic) and SM-DP+ server logs correlated by EID and timestamp.
per_query.prediction: LI misses require careful investigation (and formal procedures). Technical causes: (1) X1 provisioning on wrong network element. (2) User's traffic routed via different PGW than targeted. (3) Encrypted bearer content (LI may only get metadata). (4) SGi-LAN tap missing the flow. This requires coordination with LEA and should follow legal process.

per_query.query_text: NB-IoT device cannot complete random access procedure despite strong RSRP
per_query.reference: NB-IoT RACH failure with good coverage: (1) NPRACH configuration — check subcarrier spacing, repetition levels, and periodicity in SIB2-NB. (2) Coverage level mismatch — device may be using wrong coverage enhancement level for its RSRP. (3) Cell capacity: if NPRACH resources are exhausted (congestion), RACH fails silently. (4) Device class: Cat-NB1 vs Cat-NB2 capabilities — verify device reports correct UE category. (5) Guard band vs in-band vs standalone deployment mode — device must be configured for the correct NB-IoT deployment type. Check eNB NB-IoT RACH statistics for preamble detection rate and coverage level distribution.
per_query.prediction: UE drains battery faster than expected. Possible: (1) DRX not configured well - UE not sleeping. (2) Poor coverage forces max TX power. (3) Constant network reselection due to low RSRP. (4) Application keeping radio active (chatty heartbeats). (5) No RRC Release after idle - eNB keeping UE connected. Review DRX params and eNB inactivity timers.

per_query.query_text: IPv4v6 PDN type request rejected by PGW, UE forced to IPv4 only
per_query.reference: PDN type IPv4v6 rejection (cause code 52 = single address bearers only, or 50 = PDN type IPv6 only allowed): (1) Check PGW APN configuration — APN may only have IPv4 pool, no IPv6 prefix delegation. (2) HSS subscription: subscribed PDN type may not include IPv4v6. (3) PGW license or platform limit — some vendors require specific license for dual-stack PDN. (4) UE behavior: after rejection with cause 52 the UE should retry with IPv4 — verify the retry is successful. (5) If IPv6 is required: provision IPv6 prefix pool on PGW and update APN profile in HSS.
per_query.prediction: Three discovery methods: (1) DHCP option 120 (most common). (2) PCO in Attach (3GPP native). (3) Pre-configured on UE. If failing: verify PCO returned by PGW contains P-CSCF IPv4/v6. If using DHCP, trace DHCP discover/offer. Test: UE performs DNS SRV query for _sip._udp.<domain> - should return P-CSCF address.

per_query.query_text: Device receives ATTACH ACCEPT but immediately sends DETACH REQUEST
per_query.reference: ATTACH ACCEPT followed by immediate UE-initiated DETACH: (1) PDN connectivity failure post-attach — if default bearer establishment fails the device may detach. Check ESM cause in Activate Default EPS Bearer Context Request vs reject. (2) Device firmware issue — known bug in some chipsets where APN configuration mismatch triggers detach. (3) SIM application conflict — SIM STK applet may be overriding network selection. (4) Device detaches if IMS registration is required but fails immediately (IMS-only device). (5) Test with a different device and same SIM, and same device with a test SIM to isolate device vs subscription. Pull NAS trace from MME.
per_query.prediction: Common causes: (1) T3412 timer misconfigured - periodic TAU timer too short. (2) UE losing coverage and re-entering (check RSRP variability). (3) Battery optimization on device forcing PDN deactivate. (4) Paging DRX misalignment causing UE to miss paging and MME to detach. (5) MME-side implicit detach timer hitting.

per_query.query_text: SMS over SGd interface not delivering messages for LTE-only subscribers without CSFB
per_query.reference: SGd-based SMS (SGs-less, direct MME-to-SMSC via SGd) delivery failure: (1) SGd (Diameter) interface between MME and SMS-GMSC must be up — check Diameter peer state. (2) Subscriber must have SMS-over-SGs or SMS-over-SGd activated in HSS — check subscription flags. (3) MSISDN routing in SMS-GMSC — for MT SMS, the SMSC must route via SGd path, not MAP/CAP legacy path. (4) P-CSCF and IMS not required for SGd SMS — but verify feature flag on MME. (5) For MO SMS: check that UE initiates NAS Uplink NAS Transport with SMS payload and MME routes to SGd. Trace both Diameter SGd and NAS on MME to find the break point.
per_query.prediction: CSFB redirects to UTRAN. Failures: (1) SRVCC not actually needed here - this is CSFB, check SGs path. (2) No UTRAN coverage at UE location. (3) Gs interface between SGSN and MSC down. (4) Location Update to MSC fails (IMSI not in VLR). (5) MSC paging timer expires before UE completes RAU. Logs on MSC show final cause.

per_query.query_text: Voice call audio drops out for first 2 seconds then recovers on every call
per_query.reference: Systematic 2-second audio gap at call start points to dedicated bearer establishment timing. (1) Measure time between SIP 200 OK and QCI 1 dedicated bearer activation — if > 1s, bearer setup is the culprit. (2) Jitter buffer pre-fill: some MGWs/UEs buffer before playing — check jitter buffer configuration. (3) Early media / ringback timing — is audio gate opening before RTP arrives? (4) RTCP negotiation delay on SBC — some SBCs wait for RTCP before opening audio. (5) SRTP key exchange — if DTLS or SDES handshake takes > 1s, media is delayed. Capture RTP at P-CSCF and UE simultaneously and measure first-packet timestamp.
per_query.prediction: One-way audio = RTP flowing in one direction only. Check: (1) NAT on signaling vs media paths. (2) SBC media anchoring - SDP c= line pointing to unreachable IP. (3) Firewall blocking RTP on one side. (4) MGW codec mismatch - re-INVITE for codec change failed. (5) Capture RTP streams at SBC to confirm flow direction.

per_query.query_text: MIMO rank-2 throughput significantly worse than rank-1 for stationary UEs
per_query.reference: Rank-2 performing worse than rank-1 for stationary UEs indicates spatial channel issues: (1) Antenna cross-correlation too high — if physical antenna separation is insufficient, rank-2 spatial streams interfere. (2) Antenna port calibration mismatch — check RF calibration on both TX ports. (3) Precoding matrix indicator (PMI) feedback from UE — stationary UE should report stable PMI. If PMI is unstable, check UE feedback or downlink channel estimation. (4) CSI-RS configuration — incorrect CSI pilot power prevents accurate channel estimation. (5) UE receiver capability: some devices have poor rank-2 implementation. Test with a reference UE to isolate.
per_query.prediction: High RRC re-est rate = UEs losing RRC connection (radio link failure) and trying to resume. Indicates: (1) Coverage holes - UEs moving out of range. (2) Interference bursts. (3) Too-aggressive handover parameters causing HOF. (4) eNB software issue dropping contexts. Target <1% of total connections; >3% needs investigation.

per_query.query_text: HSS returning Error-User-Unknown for valid IMSI during TAU procedure
per_query.reference: HSS Diameter error DIAMETER_ERROR_USER_UNKNOWN (5001) on S6a Update Location Request during TAU: (1) IMSI provisioned in HSS? Check directly in HSS subscriber DB — provisioning error is common. (2) IMSI format mismatch — HSS may store with/without leading zeros. (3) If moving between MMEs (inter-MME TAU) — old MME's IMSI de-registration may not have reached HSS. (4) HSS replication lag in geo-redundant setups — subscriber created on primary, TAU hit secondary before replication. (5) Subscription state: IMSI may be marked inactive in HSS (e.g. SIM swap in progress). Check HSS audit logs for the specific IMSI with full trace.
per_query.prediction: Symptoms: high S1-AP processing delay, attach rejections with cause 22 (congestion). Steps: (1) CPU and memory on MME nodes. (2) S1-AP message rate - compare to capacity. (3) Pool balancing - is one MME hotter than others? (4) Diameter S6a response time from HSS. (5) Enable MME overload protection (reject low-priority traffic). (6) Long-term: scale horizontally.
